record.context_brief: Adjoints for forgetful functors from Boolean inverse semigroups
record.original_question: Does the forgetful functor from Boolean inverse semigroups to left-handed skew Boolean algebras have a left adjoint, and if so how is it constructed? What is the analogous answer for Boolean inverse ∧-semigroups and left-handed skew Boolean intersection algebras?

evidence.quote: There is a forgetful functor from Boolean inverse semigroups to LSBAs
Does it have a left adjoint? Then how is it constructed?
A similar question can be asked also about Boolean inverse ∧-semigroups and LSBIAs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Boolean inverse semigroup is an inverse semigroup S with zero such that the semilattice of idempotents E(S) is a (generalized) Boolean algebra and such that any pair of compatible elements (elements a, b with a*b and ab* both idempotent) admits a join in the natural partial order; morphisms are semigroup homomorphisms preserving 0 and finite compatible joins. A Boolean inverse ∧-semigroup is a Boolean inverse semigroup in which any two elements admit a meet in the natural partial order; morphisms additionally preserve meets.

A left-handed skew Boolean algebra (LSBA) is an algebra (A; ∧, ∨, \, 0) such that (A; ∧, ∨) is a left-handed strongly distributive skew lattice with zero (i.e., x ∧ (y ∨ z) = (x ∧ y) ∨ (x ∧ z), (x ∨ y) ∧ x = x, x ∧ y ∧ x = x ∧ y, etc.) and \ is a relative complement satisfying (x \ y) ∧ y = 0 = y ∧ (x \ y) and (x \ y) ∨ (x ∧ y ∧ x) = x. A left-handed skew Boolean intersection algebra (LSBIA) is an LSBA equipped with an additional binary "intersection" operation ∩ which is the meet for the natural partial order x ≤ y ⇔ x ∧ y = x = y ∧ x.

Every Boolean inverse semigroup S has an underlying LSBA obtained by retaining the operations ∧ (multiplication-based meet via idempotent structure), the compatible join ∨ restricted to the appropriate context, the relative complement, and 0; this gives a forgetful functor U: BoolInvSgp → LSBA. Similarly, a forgetful functor U^∧: BoolInv∧Sgp → LSBIA is defined on Boolean inverse ∧-semigroups.

Questions:
(1) Does U: BoolInvSgp → LSBA admit a left adjoint, and if so give an explicit construction of this left adjoint.
(2) Does U^∧: BoolInv∧Sgp → LSBIA admit a left adjoint, and if so give an explicit construction.
artifact.category_tag: Boolean inverse semigroups and skew Boolean algebras
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches reveal substantial closely related work — notably the Booleanization construction giving a left adjoint to the forgetful functor from Boolean inverse semigroups to inverse semigroups with zero, and noncommutative Stone-type dualities involving left-handed skew Boolean algebras and étale groupoids (Kudryavtseva–Lawson, Bauer–Cvetko-Vah, Lawson–Lenz, Resende). However, no source explicitly settles the existence and construction of a left adjoint to the forgetful functor from Boolean inverse semigroups to LSBAs, nor the analogous statement for Boolean inverse ∧-semigroups and LSBIAs. The status is therefore unclear from the publicly available literature.

status_evidence.title: The Booleanization of an inverse semigroup
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs a left adjoint (Booleanization) to the forgetful functor from Boolean inverse semigroups to inverse semigroups with zero.
status_evidence.claim: Related adjoint construction exists for a different forgetful functor, but not directly for the LSBA forgetful functor.

status_evidence.title: Boolean sets, skew Boolean algebras and a non-commutative Stone duality
status_evidence.snippet: Develops dualities for skew Boolean algebras via presheaves over Boolean algebras.
status_evidence.claim: Provides categorical machinery for LSBAs relevant to the question, without resolving the specific adjoint.

status_evidence.title: Free Skew Boolean Algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs free skew Boolean algebras, relevant to potential free/left adjoint constructions.
status_evidence.claim: Provides free-object techniques but does not address the specific forgetful functor in question.
